states.label: A · Queue: batch 1 of 3, sized to what Claude can read in full; the rest wait for the batches that start right after
B · Live log: two reads came back short; Distill asked for the exact lines, then checks each page against its source
C · Review: read in full, detail check and archive are information, not a decision
D · Review: 2 sources didn’t finish in this session; they go to a fresh session as the next part
E · Hard stop: a file Distill can’t decode is not in the change; Approve counts only the others
F · After the batch: the file waits under Held in inbox/ with Try again

boards.title: Full reads · every source read to its last line, checked by Distill
boards.heading: Full reads: Distill checks every line was read, and fixes it itself
boards.intro: “Relying on human is wrong.” A 22-note batch was read in one session: Claude read 8 files whole and only the first 110 lines of 14, and two of the 8 “whole” reads were cut off by the tool without an error. Now a batch takes only as much text as one session can read in full (the rest start right after), Distill counts the lines each Read returned, and when lines are missing it asks the same session for exactly those lines. What still doesn’t finish goes to a fresh session as the next part. Each page is then checked against its source at the detail you chose, and what is missing is added before you see it. Review shows all of this as information. Only a file Distill can’t decode reaches you, and it is never part of what you approve. Originals are archived in the vault with each batch, so clearing inbox/ loses nothing. Pages made before this are read again automatically.
